Deliver the macOS local entry and one reviewed runtime build.

## Scope

- Provide the macOS launch and safe reopen entry
- Separate reading-session close from owned service stop

## Entry conditions

- Shared reading views and service contract are integrated.

## Exit criteria

- Launch/reopen/session/stop ownership is implemented and the exact final frontend package passes the existing static/build publication path.

## Risks

## TASK-011 - Provide the macOS launch and safe reopen entry

Add a project-relative Launch Project.command and static Project App Setup.html. The launcher selects an already prepared Python runtime/package, starts the owned Project-app service, waits for authenticated readiness, and opens Home; compatible running instances are reopened only after exact project/package/instance verification.

| Dependencies | TASK-010 |
| Parallel group | None |
| Completed at | None |

### Risks

- Preserve paths with spaces and confine transient descriptors and credentials to private app-owned runtime files.
- Do not install or discover a runtime by executing arbitrary project code.

### Acceptance criteria

- Double-click on the initially supported macOS host needs no typed command and opens the selected launcher-relative project Home after readiness.
- Missing Python or invalid package opens readable local setup guidance without depending on Python, npm, a cloud asset or a depot service.
- Reopen validates ownership and exact compatibility; stale descriptors, reused PIDs and occupied ports never authorize connecting to another project or killing unrelated processes.

### Planned verification

- Inspect shell quoting, launcher-relative root selection, executable-mode requirements and ownership handshake; include actual launch/reopen in TASK-018 and only uncovered lifecycle cases in TASK-017.

## TASK-012 - Separate reading-session close from owned service stop

Add an authenticated Stop app action limited to the verified Project-app service and clear Close reading session behavior. Reuse current credential and response-invalidating controls, with no timeout added to active reading sessions.

| Dependencies | TASK-011 |
| Parallel group | None |

### Risks

- Service controls change app-owned transient state only and must not become general browser execution authority.

### Acceptance criteria

- Tab closure, explicit session revocation and owned service shutdown have distinct accurate effects; the UI explains effects on other tabs.
- Stop cannot target Tasks, agents, watchers, independent backends or unrelated processes, and uncertain shutdown is reported honestly.
- Package replacement requires restart, and late/revoked responses cannot restore content after close/stop.

### Planned verification

- Review authenticated shutdown dispatch and session invalidation; reuse existing unaffected session tests and cover delivered controls once in TASK-018.

### Risks

- Verify prepared toolchain availability before execution; an absent prerequisite does not authorize installation.
- Do not weaken manifest closure/CSP or revive an authoring bundle to simplify packaging.

### Acceptance criteria

- One build supports Project-app and standalone Explorer modes and binds the exact source, schema, toolchain and local assets in the existing publication scheme.
- Runtime launch does not install/build or fetch remote assets; incomplete and changed packages fail with bounded guidance.
- The recorded static/build result is reused for distribution and final verification; rerun only when material source changes invalidate it.

### Planned verification

- From SKILLS-depo/ontology/explorer, with EXPLORER_PYTHON set to the existing project Python, run npm run build followed by npm run package:runtime; inspect the resulting manifest and source/build receipt.
